comments.title: Initial AE Design Coordination Meeting Not Documented
comments.comment: Documentation of the initial coordination meeting with Austin Energy Design covering permanent electric service requirements cannot be verified from the available project files.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2 requires initial coordination with AE Design before site plan approval, covering projected electrical loads, transformer locations, underground cabling routing, meter locations, and additional required facilities. Sheet 21 shows a preliminary electrical design and Sheet 3 contains AE boilerplate language and contact information, but no ESPA correspondence, design meeting notes, or initial coordination documentation is present in the accessible project files. The Master Comment Report references an AE Bluebeam review link and notes the completeness check is complete, but neither satisfies the requirement to document an initial coordination discussion of these specific topics.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.resolution: Submit documentation of the initial coordination meeting with Austin Energy Design, including records of discussions covering permanent electric service requirements, projected electrical loads, transformer locations, underground cabling routing, meter locations, and any additional required facilities. Contact information for Austin Energy reviewers (Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153; Rosemary Avila, rosemary.avila@austinenergy.com) is noted on the plans.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Unclear status (2/3 runs) — reviewer should verify whether ESPA correspondence or initial coordination meeting notes exist in the AE Design project file or Bluebeam session.

perRunFindings.comment: Initial coordination with AE Design to discuss permanent electric service requirements, projected electrical loads, transformer locations, underground cabling routing, meter locations, and additional required facilities must be documented with AE Design approval before site plan approval.

While Master Comment Report acknowledges AE Design review process is underway (Bluebeam link provided), no evidence of initial coordination meeting discussing service requirements, loads, transformer locations, routing, meter locations, and facilities was located. The completeness check status shows AE review is pending, not completed. Cannot confirm that initial coordination with AE Design discussing permanent electric service requirements, loads, transformer locations, routing, and meter locations was completed per UCM § 1.4.2.

perRunFindings.comment: Initial coordination meeting with Austin Energy Design to discuss service requirements, loads, transformer locations, underground cabling routing, and meter locations cannot be verified from the available site plan and correspondence. The Bluebeam link is referenced but the actual comments are not accessible in the provided materials.

comments.title: Preliminary Electrical Design Lacks Formal AE Design Approval and Approval Correspondence
comments.comment: Sheet 21 is explicitly labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no AE Design approval stamp or notation, and no proof of Austin Energy Design approval correspondence has been submitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2 requires two things prior to site plan approval: (1) the preliminary electric service design must be formally reviewed and approved by AE Design, and (2) proof of the approval correspondence must be submitted. Neither has been satisfied. The plan carries a 'PRELIMINARY' label with no approval stamp, signature, or approval notation. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam link for AE site comments and confirms the AE completeness check is complete (per Victor Givens), but neither constitutes formal design review approval. No approval letter, approval email, or signed design review documentation from Austin Energy Design is present in the accessible project files.
comments.resolution: Obtain formal design review approval from the Austin Energy Design business unit for the preliminary electrical design shown on Sheet 21, then submit the approval letter or written approval correspondence with the site plan resubmittal. A completeness check confirmation alone does not satisfy this requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Preliminary electric service design must be formally reviewed and approved by AE Design before site plan approval. Obtain design approval from Austin Energy Design business unit and provide approval correspondence.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' - explicitly indicating it is preliminary, not formally designed or approved. Master Comment Report (section 02-electric-review.md) references AE Design review via Bluebeam markup but provides only a link to comments (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), not approval correspondence. No dated AE Design approval letter, design review completion documentation, or formal approval correspondence was located in supplementary documents. Completeness check shows 'AE completeness check complete' but this is not the same as formal design review approval.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The plan is explicitly labeled 'PRELIMINARY' which means the formal design review and approval process with AE Design has not been completed. UCM § 1.4.2 requires preliminary design to be 'formally reviewed and approved by AE Design prior to site plan approval.' Completeness check completion is not the same as design approval. The Master Comment Report acknowledges AE Design review is pending (via Bluebeam comments), but no approval documentation has been provided. This is a clear deficiency - the design is still in preliminary status.

perRunFindings.comment: Preliminary electrical design not showing formal Austin Energy Design approval. No approval letter, approval stamp, or design approval documentation is visible on Sheet 21 or in accessible project correspondence. Completeness check completion is not equivalent to design approval.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 is explicitly labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no Austin Energy Design approval stamp, signature, or approval notation. The Master Comment Report references Austin Energy Design Criteria requirements and mentions a Bluebeam link for 'AE site comments' but does not provide evidence of formal design approval. No approval letter from Austin Energy Design business unit is present in the available site plan or correspondence files. The completeness check indicates only that Austin Energy completeness review is complete, not that design approval has been granted.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The requirement is for 'Preliminary electric service design [to be] formally reviewed and approved by AE Design prior to site plan approval.' The design shown is preliminary, but there is no evidence of formal review and approval by Austin Energy Design. A completeness check is not the same as design approval. The absence of an approval stamp, approval letter, or approval reference in the accessible documentation indicates this requirement has not been met. The fact that Austin Energy Design Criteria were cited suggests requirements were acknowledged, but does not demonstrate approval of the actual design.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electrical design. This must include design review approval from AE Design business unit, not just completeness check confirmation.
perRunFindings.observation: No AE Design approval correspondence found in project files. Master Comment Report references Bluebeam review comments link but no approval letter, design review completion letter, or formal correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electrical design was located. Engineer's Summary Letter does not mention electric service. Completeness check results show only that 'AE completeness check complete' from Victor Givens, not design review approval.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2 requires 'Proof of correspondence from AE Design approving preliminary electric design' to be submitted. The absence of any AE Design approval letter, approval correspondence, or signed design review documentation is a direct non-compliance. Completeness check confirmation is an administrative milestone, not design approval. Master Comment Report indicates design review is still pending/in process (Bluebeam comments awaiting response).

perRunFindings.comment: Proof of Austin Energy Design approval correspondence not submitted with site plan. No approval letter or approval email from Austin Energy Design is visible in the available documentation.
perRunFindings.observation: No proof of correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electric design is visible on the site plan cover sheet, general notes, or in the accessible supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam link for Austin Energy comments but does not provide a formal approval letter. The completeness check documentation only confirms that Austin Energy completeness review is complete (by Victor Givens), not that design approval has been submitted or received.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The requirement explicitly states 'Proof of correspondence from AE Design approving preliminary electric design [must be] submitted.' This proof must be submitted with the site plan documents. The absence of an approval letter, approval email, or correspondence in the available documentation represents a failure to meet this requirement. comments.title: Design Change Re-Coordination with AE Design Not Confirmed
comments.comment: Whether the current electric design represents changes from a previously AE-reviewed design, and whether those changes were re-coordinated with Austin Energy Design, cannot be determined from the available project documentation.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2 requires that any changes to electric requirements or design made since a previous submittal be re-coordinated with and re-approved by AE Design. The site plan submittal date is May 20, 2025, but no revision history, prior submission electric design, change logs, or re-coordination correspondence is accessible in the project files. Applicability of this requirement depends on whether a prior submittal included an AE-reviewed or AE-approved electric design.

If this is the first electric design submittal, note that on the plan or in a cover letter.

comments.title: AE-Approved Electric Design Not Reflected on Site Plan, Wet Utilities, and Landscape Sheets
comments.comment: The AE-approved electric service design has not been incorporated into the site plan, wet utilities plan, or landscape plan as required prior to site plan approval.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.4.2 requires the AE-approved electric service design to be reflected on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. The following deficiencies exist:
- Site plan (Sheet 9): Electric service routing, transformer locations, and meter locations are absent from the main site plan; the design remains only on the preliminary electrical sheet (Sheet 21).
- Wet utilities plan (Sheet 19): It cannot be confirmed that approved electric routing is shown alongside water/wastewater infrastructure; Sheet 19 cross-references Sheet 21 profiles but full electric design reflection is not verified.
- Landscape plan (Sheet 31): Transformer pad locations and required clearance zones shown on Sheet 21 have not been confirmed on the landscape plan, and no clearance notation is visible.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 19); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.resolution: After receiving AE Design approval: (1) add the approved transformer locations, underground routing, and meter locations to the main site plan (Sheet 9); (2) confirm or add approved electric infrastructure routing to the wet utilities plan (Sheet 19); (3) confirm that all four transformer pad locations and required clearance zones are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) with no conflicting planting within AE-required clearances.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Landscape plan updates (Sheet 31) may require coordination with the landscape reviewer to confirm transformer clearances are respected in the planting design.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: EL-8.8 (Sheet 9) is a confirmed fail; EL-8.9 (Sheet 19) and EL-8.10 (Sheet 31) are unclear pending direct sheet examination.

comments.title: Point of Electric Service Not Labeled on Electrical Plan
comments.comment: The specific point of electric service — where Austin Energy's facilities end and the customer's facilities begin — is not identified or labeled on Sheet 21.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2 requires the point of electric service to be shown on the site plan and approved by AE Design. Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines originating from the Valley View Road right-of-way but does not explicitly mark or label the service demarcation point. Sheet 3 general notes reference AE contact information and easement requirements but do not identify the specific service connection point. No ESPA determination letter identifying the approved service point is present in the accessible project documentation.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: Service entry point from Valley View Road right-of-way
comments.resolution: Label the point of electric service on Sheet 21 at the demarcation location where Austin Energy's facilities end and customer facilities begin. Obtain AE Design confirmation of the service point location (typically established through the ESPA process) and reference the ESPA determination in the plan notes or general notes.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service on Sheet 21 (where Austin Energy facilities end and customer facilities begin). Obtain approval from Austin Energy Design confirming the service point location.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric line entering from the west (Valley View Road right-of-way) but does not explicitly label or identify the 'Point of Service' - the demarcation point where Austin Energy responsibility ends and customer responsibility begins. Vision analysis confirmed: 'The exact technical demarcation point where utility responsibility ends and private service begins is not specifically identified by a label.' The point of service is a critical element that must be shown and approved by AE Design.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item requires 'Point of electric service not shown on site plan or not approved by AE Design group' per UCM § 1.4.2. While the service routing is shown, the specific point of service demarcation is not labeled. This is required to be clearly identified on the plan and approved by AE Design. This is a clear deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Point of electric service not explicitly marked or labeled on site plan. Specific service connection point to Austin Energy system not shown or approved by Austin Energy Design.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines originating from Valley View Road on the left side of the site, but the specific point of service (the connection point to the existing Austin Energy system) is not explicitly marked or labeled on the preliminary design. Sheet 3 contains general Austin Energy notes but does not identify the specific point of service. perRunFindings.reasoning: The requirement states 'Point of electric service [must be] shown on site plan or [must be] approved by AE Design group.' The preliminary design shows the general routing from Valley View Road but does not explicitly mark and label the specific point of service connection. Per the grouping's Regulatory Overview, the ESPA process 'determines technical requirements including service type...and whether line extension fees apply.' comments.title: Underground Electric Infrastructure Specifications Absent from Electrical Plan
comments.comment: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing but lacks required specifications for duct banks, pull boxes, and underground cabling needed for AE Design review and approval.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.4.2 requires underground electric infrastructure details to meet AE requirements and be approved by AE Design. The following specifications are missing from the preliminary electrical design on Sheet 21:
- Duct bank materials, sizing, installation details, and protection requirements for underground routing
- Electric service pull box and vault locations, types, and specifications (callouts are shown but no design details provided)
- Underground cabling types, conduit requirements, burial depths, clearances from other utilities, and road crossing requirements
comments.resolution: In coordination with Austin Energy Design, add to Sheet 21: (1) duct bank specifications including materials, sizing, and installation details; (2) pull box and vault locations with type designations and specifications; and (3) underground cabling details including cable type, conduit sizing, burial depths, clearances from other utilities, and road crossing details. All specifications must meet AE Design requirements and be included as part of the AE Design approval submittal.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify whether duct bank, pull box, and routing specifications appear on Sheet 21 or in supplemental detail sheets before requiring resubmittal.
